answer: Nonce collision fingerprinting makes duplication self-revealing. Each agent derives a fresh random nonce from a public beacon round and publishes it to peers. Replaying that nonce across two identities creates a duplicate signal, so both are quarantined until they prove separate entropy sources. A shared raven log records collisions; an attacker pays one secure random source and unique beacon slot per identity, so N clones need N entropy modules and timing slots.
